title: A Parish for the Verdict
premise: Yara Halloran, archivist of St. Brannoc's Cathedral, receives two letters on the same morning: one confessing to a thirty-year-old death in the locked crypt, the other promising a second confession if she keeps silent. As she investigates, Yara discovers the victim was not who the town believed — he was her own father, living under another name, and the trial that convicted an innocent man was engineered by the cathedral's canons to protect their land holdings. The confessing letter-writer is the dying former verger, but the true architect is Bishop's registrar Edmund Vase, now a beloved civic pillar. At the pre-trial hearing, Yara trades the archive's sealed evidence for Vase's confession, choosing truth over the institution that gave her shelter, and the crypt is finally opened.
about_author: Odile Ishikawa spent a decade cataloguing ecclesiastical archives in coastal England before turning to fiction full-time. Her mysteries are known for their patient, paper-trail suspense and their tenderness toward people who survive by keeping quiet.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Postmark
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On an ordinary Tuesday, two letters arrive with identical postmarks: one confessing to a killing in the cathedral crypt thirty years ago, one warning her to burn the first. She files neither. Emotional beat: the thrill of a secret that finally belongs to her.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She surveys the crypt door, sealed since 1994 by order of the then-dean, and finds the old key register altered — a page razored out. Emotional beat: unease; the archive she trusted has been edited.

chapters.title: What the Verger Kept
chapters.summary: Yara visits Tom Pellowe, the retired verger, who denies everything but his hands shake over his tea. He mentions 'the arrangement' and stops himself. Emotional beat: pity warring with suspicion.

chapters.title: Alibi of the Canons
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, digging through 1994 records. Every canon claims to have been at a diocesan retreat the night Daniel Merrick vanished — a retreat whose guest book is missing. Emotional beat: the pattern of coordinated silence emerging.

chapters.title: A Name Not Her Own
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A baptismal record reveals Daniel Merrick lived under the alias Daniel Halloran — her father, who abandoned her as a child and died, supposedly elsewhere, the year she started at the cathedral. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case is personal.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A third letter arrives, addressed in her father's handwriting though he is dead: 'Ask Tom about the harvest night.' Someone has access to his old papers. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tom Breaks a Little
chapters.summary: Tom Pellowe's POV. Dying of heart failure, Tom recalls the harvest-night argument between young Edmund Vase and Daniel over parish land deeds, and how he helped carry something heavy down the crypt stairs. He stops before the end. Emotional beat: guilt as a physical weight.

chapters.title: Edmund Vase, Pillar of the Town
chapters.summary: Yara interviews Vase under the pretext of donating his papers to the archive. Charming, generous, untouchable — he praises her father's memory without knowing she knows. Emotional beat: revulsion masked as courtesy.

chapters.title: The Trial That Convicted Nobody
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Court archives show a handyman, Silas Crane, convicted of manslaughter in absentia after fleeing; he drowned before appeal. But the forensic report contradicts the verdict's timeline. Emotional beat: cold anger at machinery working as designed.

chapters.title: Silas Crane's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Ruth Crane, a solicitor's clerk, contacts Yara anonymously — she has spent years pulling the same threads. They meet; Ruth's father died branded a killer. Emotional beat: alliance forged from shared damage.

chapters.title: The Dean's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the restricted ledger she finds payments from the cathedral trust to 'P.V.' for seven years after the death — hush money to someone. The current dean begs her to leave it be. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised her.

chapters.title: Harvest Night, Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Alternating Yara/Ruth. Using weather logs, receipts, and a photograph, they rebuild the night: Daniel confronted Vase about forged deeds; three canons helped subdue him; the crypt was never meant to hold a body permanently. Emotional beat: grim clarity.

chapters.title: Someone Is Filing My Office
chapters.summary: Yara returns to find her office searched, folders re-shelved millimeters off. Only one person alphabetizes like that: herself — or whoever trained beside her. Suspicion falls on her mentor, Canon Averil. Emotional beat: paranoia inside a sanctuary.

chapters.title: Averil's Confession of Sorts
chapters.summary: Canon Averil's POV. She admits she was the retreat's organizer — there was no retreat; it was cover. She protected the church, believing Daniel a blackmailer, and has regretted it for thirty years. She will not testify. Emotional beat: the banality of complicity.

chapters.title: The Key Register Forged
chapters.summary: Yara proves the razored page hid Vase's signature checking out the crypt key the night Daniel died. She photographs everything and hides copies in plain sight among uncatalogued boxes. Emotional beat: quiet triumph, quickly shadowed.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Vase offers her a funded fellowship abroad — leave before the anniversary service and the past stays past. She declines. That night the archive's sprinkler system 'malfunctions' above her office. Emotional beat: terror wearing gloves.

chapters.title: Tom's Last Statement
chapters.summary: Tom Pellowe's POV. Given days to live, Tom dictates a full statement to Ruth: what was carried, who ordered it, where the body lies beneath the crypt floor's third slab. He signs. Emotional beat: release, and dread of what it will cost.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the pre-trial inquest review, Vase's counsel moves to suppress the statement as hearsay from a dying man. Yara produces the key register and the trust ledger. The judge orders the crypt opened. Emotional beat: the room tilting toward truth.

chapters.title: Third Slab
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Before officials, witnesses, and cameras, the slab is raised. Below: remains with a healed childhood fracture matching Daniel Halloran's hospital records — her father, found at last. Emotional beat: grief arriving thirty years late.

chapters.title: Vase Unraveling
chapters.summary: Vase's POV. Confronted with the ledger, the register, and Averil's wavering loyalty, Vase calculates, bargains, then confesses on tape — not to murder, he insists, but to 'an accident we chose not to report.' His empire of respectability collapses in a single afternoon. Emotional beat: power exposed as costume.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Vase and two surviving canons are committed for trial; Silas Crane's conviction is posthumously quashed, and Ruth reads a statement in her father's name. Yara testifies last, steady, naming the price everyone paid for silence. Emotional beat: justice as accounting, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: An Open Crypt, An Open Door
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. She buries her father properly, resigns her post, and accepts Ruth's offer to consult on cold cases. The crypt becomes a memorial chapel. Final letter in her drawer, unsigned: 'Thank you for keeping the files.' Emotional beat: survival, at last, feeling like more than survival.
